issue: When ruling on a motion for a sentence reduction under § 404 of the First Step Act, must the district court consider the 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) sentencing factors?
provision: First Step Act of 2018, Pub. L. 115-391, § 404

sides.position: Yes, the district court must consider the § 3553(a) factors when ruling on a § 404 motion.
cases: United States v. Easter, 975 F.3d 318 (3d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Chambers, 956 F.3d 667 (4th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Boulding, 960 F.3d 774 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. White, 984 F.3d 76 (D.C. Cir. 2020)
United States v. Lawrence, No. 20-3061, 2021 WL 2425959 (D.C. Cir. June 15, 2021)

sides.position: No, the district court is not required to consider the § 3553(a) factors when ruling on a § 404 motion.
cases: United States v. Concepcion, 991 F.3d 279 (1st Cir. 2021)
United States v. Moore, 963 F.3d 725 (8th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Moyhernandez, 5 F.4th 195 (2d Cir. 2021)

this_court: No, the district court is not required to consider the § 3553(a) factors when ruling on a § 404 motion.
quote: The Third, Fourth, Sixth, and D.C. Circuits require consideration of the § 3553(a) factors; the First, Eighth, Tenth, and Eleventh Circuits, along with the Ninth Circuit (in an unpublished decision), rule that consideration of those factors is not required.
cite: United States v. Moyhernandez, 5 F.4th 195 (2d Cir. 2021)
